subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters on embedded agent turns, and should that happen via https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 or a replacement?
rationale: The source-level repeated-normalization problem is clear, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, custom providers, plugin metadata lifecycle, and the broader prepared-runtime direction.

options.title: Refresh and land bounded cache
options.body: Use the existing PR or a narrow replacement to cache cloned schema parameters only for safe bundled normalizers while rebuilding fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared-runtime migration
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime work carries enough stable provider/tool facts to remove repeated hot-path normalization without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live Google proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main live Google/Gemini or heap evidence confirms the user-visible ban, hang, or allocation impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land bounded cache
recommendation.body: Use the existing PR or a narrow replacement to cache cloned schema parameters only for safe bundled normalizers while rebuilding fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows repeated work on provider-tools, provider handle reuse, runtime-plan tools, and the internalized agent runtime boundary affected by this decision.
